rows.text: A colourless ramp deck whose payoff is not damage but permanents. Annihilator does not care about life totals, blockers or lifegain — it takes lands, rocks and enchantments off the board until an opponent simply cannot function. The deck's job is to reach eight or ten mana two turns before anyone expects it, and Kozilek's own text turns every uncastable fatty in your hand into a hard counterspell while you get there.

rows.name: Kozilek, the Great Distortion
rows.text: refills your hand to seven on cast, and then every card in that hand is a counterspell for a spell of matching mana value. In a deck full of eight- and ten-drops, that covers most of what a table casts.

rows.name: Zhulodok, Void Gorger
rows.text: every colourless spell of mana value seven or more you cast FROM HAND gets cascade twice. Casting one Eldrazi becomes casting three spells. He is the biggest single upgrade in the deck.

rows.name: Conduit of Ruin
rows.text: tutors a colourless seven-drop to the top of your library, and makes your first creature each turn cost two less. Cast it on turn four and the following turn is enormous.

rows.name: Endless One
rows.text: the flexible body that is a two-drop when you are behind and a 10/10 when you are not.

guide.title: Ramp, and a lot of it

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: turn one, every time.

rows.name: Mana Vault
rows.text: three mana on turn one, and the untap cost rarely matters in a deck that wants to tap out anyway.

rows.name: Grim Monolith
rows.text: the same, with a cheaper cast.

rows.name: Basalt Monolith
rows.text: three mana that untaps for three, so it is a mana sink as well.

rows.name: Metalworker
rows.text: two colourless per artifact card revealed from hand. With a normal hand that is six or eight mana from a three-drop, on turn four.

rows.name: Thran Dynamo
rows.text: three, reliably.

rows.name: Gilded Lotus
rows.text: three of any colour, which matters only for the few coloured pips in the deck.

rows.name: Chromatic Orrery
rows.text: five mana and a draw engine.

rows.name: Hedron Archive
rows.text: two mana, or two cards when the game goes long.

rows.name: Dreamstone Hedron
rows.text: three mana, or three cards.

rows.name: Worn Powerstone
rows.text: two, and it is cheap enough to matter on turn three.

rows.name: Sisay's Ring
rows.text: two more.

rows.name: Ur-Golem's Eye
rows.text: two more again. The redundancy is the point.

rows.name: Everflowing Chalice
rows.text: scales to whatever you have spare.

rows.name: Palladium Myr
rows.text: two mana on a body, so Metalworker and Kuldotha Forgemaster can use it.

rows.name: Foundry Inspector
rows.text: a discount on every artifact in the deck.

rows.name: Unwinding Clock
rows.text: untaps every rock during each opponent's untap step. It turns a board of mana rocks into instant-speed mana on four turns instead of one.

rows.name: Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre
rows.text: destroys a permanent on cast, is indestructible, and annihilator 4 removes four permanents on every attack.

rows.name: Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger
rows.text: exiles two permanents on cast and mills twenty per attack — a legitimate alternate win.

rows.name: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth
rows.text: four cards on cast and annihilator 4, and it shuffles your graveyard back in when it dies.

rows.name: Pathrazer of Ulamog
rows.text: annihilator 3, and it cannot be blocked except by three or more creatures.

rows.name: Artisan of Kozilek
rows.text: reanimates a creature on cast, then annihilator 2 every attack.

rows.name: Spawnsire of Ulamog
rows.text: annihilator 1, and it makes Eldrazi Spawn to ramp toward the next one.

rows.name: Bane of Bala Ged
rows.text: exiles two of their permanents on every attack, which dodges every "when this dies" trigger annihilator gives them.

rows.name: Void Winnower
rows.text: opponents cannot cast spells with EVEN mana values, and cannot block with even-cost creatures. Against most decks that is half their library turned off.

rows.name: It That Betrays
rows.text: whenever an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent, YOU get it. Alongside any annihilator creature, every attack hands you their best lands and rocks. This is the deck's ceiling.

rows.name: All Is Dust
rows.text: every permanent you control is colourless. It is a board wipe that leaves you with everything.

rows.name: Ugin, the Spirit Dragon
rows.text: the minus exiles only COLOURED permanents, so it is another one-sided sweeper, and the ultimate rebuilds your entire board.

rows.name: Karn Liberated
rows.text: exiles any permanent every other turn, and strips their hand in between.

rows.name: Titan's Presence
rows.text: three mana to exile almost any creature, using the fatties in your hand as fuel.

rows.name: Warping Wail
rows.text: one mana of real interaction — a small creature, a sorcery, or a mana Scion.

rows.name: Scour from Existence
rows.text: exiles anything at instant speed. Expensive, but unconditional.

rows.name: Thought-Knot Seer
rows.text: takes their best card and blanks the turn they were building toward.

rows.name: Spine of Ish Sah
rows.text: destroys any permanent on entry, and returns to your hand whenever it hits the graveyard. Sacrifice it to Kuldotha Forgemaster and you get it back.

rows.name: Kuldotha Forgemaster
rows.text: three artifacts — the rocks you have already spent — becomes any artifact in the deck, straight onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Meteor Golem
rows.text: another destroy-on-entry body.

rows.name: Duplicant
rows.text: exiles a creature and becomes it.

rows.name: Steel Hellkite
rows.text: flies, and after it connects it destroys every nonland permanent at the mana value of your choosing. Against a token deck, name zero.

rows.name: Scrap Trawler
rows.text: every artifact that dies buys back a cheaper one.

rows.name: Darksteel Forge
rows.text: every artifact you control becomes indestructible, which with this many rocks makes you immune to most wraths.

rows.name: Wurmcoil Engine
rows.text: deathtouch, lifelink, and two 3/3s when it dies.

rows.name: Myr Battlesphere
rows.text: five bodies and a damage burst on attack.

rows.name: Solemn Simulacrum
rows.text: a land and a card.

rows.name: Expedition Map
rows.text: finds Ancient Tomb or whichever utility land the board needs.

rows.name: Crucible of Worlds
rows.text: replays the lands that annihilator and All Is Dust cost you.

rows.name: Mind Stone
rows.text: ramp early, a card late.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep two mana sources and something to do with them. Sol Ring plus Mana Vault plus any three-drop rock puts Conduit of Ruin down on turn three and a real Eldrazi on turn four or five.

Hold cheap cards for Kozilek's counter ability. A hand of nothing but ten-drops can only counter ten-drops. Keeping a Mind Stone or an Everflowing Chalice around gives you coverage of the cheap interaction people actually cast.

rows.name: Zhulodok, Void Gorger
rows.text: cast him BEFORE the fatty, always. Six mana into a ten-drop next turn with double cascade is a far bigger turn than casting the ten-drop a turn earlier alone.

rows.name: It That Betrays
rows.text: if it is on the battlefield, attack with the annihilator creature into whoever has the best board, not whoever has the lowest life. Every permanent they sacrifice becomes yours.
